prompt.role: You are an expert healthcare data analyst specializing in prior authorization (PA) policy extraction for pharmaceutical drugs. You have deep knowledge of step therapy requirements, formulary structures, and how to distinguish universal criteria from indication-specific criteria.
prompt.task:
Extract step therapy requirements for {brand} ({generics_list}) from the PA policy document below. Focus exclusively on plaque psoriasis (PsO), moderate-to-severe only.
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly 5 keys. No explanation, no preamble, no markdown formatting.
prompt.scope:
INDICATION SCOPE: Extract ONLY criteria for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PsO). Ignore all criteria for: psoriatic arthritis (PsA), Crohn's disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis (AS), hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), guttate psoriasis, pustular psoriasis, erythrodermic psoriasis, or any other non-plaque-psoriasis indication.
BRAND SCOPE: Extract criteria a patient must complete BEFORE accessing {brand}. Include BOTH universal criteria (applying to all drugs in the policy) AND indication-specific criteria (applying to plaque psoriasis). Combine via AND.

business_rules.rule:
BEFORE extracting anything, check whether {brand} is listed as a PREFERRED or PREFERRED AGENT product in this policy.
If {brand} IS preferred: the step therapy and exception criteria describe how patients access NON-PREFERRED drugs, NOT how they access {brand}. Return NA for ALL FOUR fields immediately.
Signs that {brand} is preferred: appears in a "Preferred Products" table or list, labeled "Preferred" alongside other brands. The step/exception criteria are then for accessing non-preferred products.
If {brand} is NOT preferred, proceed with remaining rules.

Combine universal criteria AND indication-specific criteria via AND logic. Total step counts = universal steps + indication-specific steps.
Universal criteria: apply to all drugs in the policy. Look for: section headers "Universal", "General Criteria", "Applies to All", "For all indications", "Initial Authorization Requirements", or criteria stated before indication subsections begin.
Indication-specific criteria: apply only to plaque psoriasis. Look under sections labeled for psoriasis, PsO, or plaque psoriasis.

When criteria are joined by OR (explicit OR, "any of the following", "ONE of the following"), apply Rule 3: use the LEAST RESTRICTIVE path — the option requiring the FEWEST total steps of that type.
MANDATORY: Before assigning any step count, scan ALL branches of OR criteria for ZERO-STEP PATHS. If ANY branch requires zero steps, that parameter = NA.
RECOGNIZED ZERO-STEP PATHS — these always yield NA for the relevant parameter:
A. SEVERITY PATHS (most common — check every policy): - "Severe active PsO (e.g., greater than 10% BSA, hands/feet/face/scalp/ genitals, intractable pruritus, serious emotional consequences)" - "Crucial body areas affected (hands, feet, face, neck, scalp, genitals/groin, intertriginous areas)" - "At least 10% BSA is affected" — NO prior treatment required - "Concomitant severe PsA (erosive disease, elevated ESR/CRP, rapidly progressive)" — allows biologic access without PsO step therapy These are 0-step paths → num_steps_generic = NA, num_steps_brands = NA
B. CONTRAINDICATION ESCAPES: - "OR has an FDA labeled contraindication to ALL conventional agents" = equal-level OR → 0 generic steps → num_steps_generic = NA - "OR has an FDA labeled contraindication to ALL [biologic/preferred] agents" = equal-level OR → 0 branded steps → num_steps_brands = NA - When a multi-agent requirement states "failure OR intolerance OR contraindication with N of the following therapies," the contraindication option means each counted agent can be met via contraindication = 0 actual drug steps → brands = NA under least-restrictive logic
C. ¥-NOTE OR FOOTNOTE BLANKET EXCEPTIONS: Scan for footnotes, ¥-notes, dagger notes (¥, †, *) at the BOTTOM or MARGIN of criteria blocks. Language like: - "For patients already established on biologic therapy OR those with >10% BSA involvement, trial and failure of [step requirements] is NOT required" - "¥ Note: Step therapy waived for established biologic patients or >10% BSA" These blanket exceptions create a 0-step path for all requirements under that note → set num_steps_generic = NA, step_phototherapy = "No"
D. CONTINUITY PATHS: - "Patient is currently being treated with the requested agent" = 0-step path for all step parameters - "Medication history indicates prior use of a biologic for PsO" = prior biologic already tried → step count may still apply for NEW patients
CRITICAL ABOUT SEVERITY PATHS: "Severe disease" OR "crucial body areas" language almost ALWAYS appears as an equal-level OR alternative alongside conventional therapy failure criteria. When present, it means: patients with severe enough disease can access {brand} WITHOUT any prior step therapy. Apply Rule 3 → return NA for the relevant step parameter.
When criteria are joined by AND, ALL requirements count cumulatively. When NO explicit connector is present, default to OR.

num_steps_brands: Count required trials of BRANDED biologic or targeted synthetic drugs that must be completed BEFORE accessing {brand}.
Counts as branded: - Any named biologic drug (Humira, Enbrel, Cosentyx, Otezla, Skyrizi, Stelara, Tremfya, any TNF inhibitor, IL inhibitor, JAK inhibitor, TYK2 inhibitor) - Drug classes described as "biologic", "targeted synthetic", or "targeted immune modulator" — even if no specific brand is named - A preferred biosimilar the patient must fail BEFORE accessing another product counts as 1 branded step - If the policy references a DRUG CLASS (e.g., "CAM antagonists", "IL-23 inhibitors") and {brand} belongs to that class, the class-level step counts as a branded step FOR {brand} - If {brand} is non-preferred and universal criteria require stepping through preferred biologic alternatives, those preferred biologics count as branded steps
Does NOT count: - {brand} itself (count steps TO reach {brand}, not {brand} itself) - Conventional/non-biologic agents (methotrexate, cyclosporine, acitretin, topicals) - Phototherapy (handled separately)
Output: integer string ("1", "2", etc.) Output "NA" if NO branded steps are required. Never output "0".

num_steps_generic: Count required trials of NON-BIOLOGIC conventional agents before accessing {brand}.
Counts as generic: - Conventional systemic agents: methotrexate (MTX), cyclosporine, acitretin - Topical agents: corticosteroids, vitamin D analogs (calcipotriene/calcitriol), tazarotene, coal tar, anthralin, calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) - Any agent described as "conventional", "non-biologic", or "traditional systemic" - If a step is required but no specific drug or biologic class is named, it defaults to a generic step
Does NOT count: - Phototherapy (UVB, PUVA) — handled in step_phototherapy - Biologic or targeted synthetic drugs
Output: integer string ("1", "2", etc.) Output "NA" if NO generic steps are required. Never output "0".

step_phototherapy:
"Yes": phototherapy is a MANDATORY step with no OR alternative at the same level. The patient MUST complete phototherapy before accessing {brand}. Only use "Yes" when phototherapy and conventional therapy are joined by AND (both required simultaneously), not when phototherapy is one option in an OR.
"No": phototherapy is NOT a mandatory step. Use "No" when: - Phototherapy appears as ONE option in an OR group (not mandatory) - Phototherapy is not mentioned as a required step - Phototherapy appears in denial/contraindication criteria - The ¥-note or severe-disease path creates a 0-step path (photo not required) - The policy has OR paths that don't require phototherapy (even if one OR branch does require it — the non-phototherapy path is less restrictive)
"NA": the policy lists no criteria at all for the indication.
AND override in drug-specific subsections: Some policies list phototherapy as optional (OR) in base criteria but a drug-specific subsection changes it to mandatory (AND) for {brand} or its class. Always check drug-specific subsections for override language such as: - "member must demonstrate failure of BOTH oral agent AND phototherapy" → Yes - "Coverage Criteria 1 through 2 are applicable; however, member must demonstrate failure of both oral agent AND phototherapy" → Yes

step_therapy_text: Capture ALL step therapy language for plaque psoriasis, combining universal and indication-specific criteria verbatim or near-verbatim. Include severity bypass language (≥10% BSA, crucial body areas) if present — this language is critical evidence for why steps may be NA. Include any ¥-notes or blanket exception language that waives step requirements. Include phototherapy language if it appears within step statements. Output "NA" if {brand} is preferred or no step therapy criteria exist.

Valid values: - step_therapy_text: Verbatim criteria text (including bypass/exception language), or "NA" - num_steps_brands: "1", "2", etc. — or "NA" if none required. NEVER "0". - num_steps_generic: "1", "2", etc. — or "NA" if none required. NEVER "0". - step_phototherapy: "Yes", "No", or "NA"

Some policies (e.g., state Medicaid formularies) apply criteria to ALL "non-preferred drugs in a class" rather than naming specific brands. If you see language like: - "Clinical criteria for approval of a PA request for non-preferred cytokine and CAM antagonist drugs used to treat psoriasis are all of the following:" - "Non-preferred agents require 90-day trials of all preferred agents"
AND {brand} appears in the NON-PREFERRED drug list for plaque psoriasis: those class-level criteria apply to {brand}. Extract them as step requirements.
When preferred drugs are explicitly listed, count the number of DISTINCT preferred drug trials required to determine num_steps_brands.

Some policies state step therapy requirements for non-preferred drugs in a HEADER or CLASSIFICATION section that appears BEFORE the numbered criteria list — not inside the numbered list itself.
Always scan introductory or classification paragraphs for statements such as: - "Non-Preferred Cytokines and CAM Antagonists: Require trial and failure of a preferred adalimumab product AND one additional preferred product" - "All non-preferred anti-TNFs require trial and failure of a preferred adalimumab product AND Enbrel"
These header-level requirements count as MANDATORY branded steps even if they do not appear in the numbered criteria. Combine with numbered criteria via AND.

MULTI-DRUG PBM POLICIES WITH A STEP TABLE: Many large multi-drug policies contain a "Step Table" or "Step Tier" grid specifying which agents require prior failures of other agents. This creates TWO separate layers of criteria that BOTH apply to {brand}:
LAYER 1 — STEP TABLE TIER: Identifies how many preferred agents must have been tried before {brand} is accessible. - Step 1a = first-line preferred agent → NO biologic prerequisite (brands=NA) - Step 1b = directed to ONE TNF inhibitor → brands=1 - Step 2 = directed to ONE Step 1 agent → brands=1 - Step 3a = directed to TWO Step 1 agents → brands=2 - Step 3b = directed to TWO Step 1 or 2 agents → brands=2 - Step 3c = directed to THREE Step 1 agents → brands=3
LAYER 2 — INDICATION CRITERIA: What the patient must have tried for PsO itself (conventional agents, phototherapy) BEFORE any biologic.
BOTH layers apply. The num_steps_brands from Layer 1 AND num_steps_generic from Layer 2 are CUMULATIVE (combined via AND).
CRITICAL: Scan the Step Table explicitly. Find which row/tier contains {brand} or {generics_list}. Extract the biologic prerequisite from that tier level. Do NOT miss the Step Table simply because the drug-specific indication criteria section is visible — BOTH layers must be checked.
ZERO-STEP ESCAPE IN STEP TABLE: If the Step Table criteria for {brand}'s tier include "OR has FDA labeled contraindication to ALL required Step N agents," that is a 0-step escape → brands=NA under Rule 3.

WRONG-SECTION EXTRACTION: In multi-drug policies, {brand} may appear in another drug's criteria as a REQUIRED PREREQUISITE (what patients must fail before getting that OTHER drug). DO NOT extract those as criteria FOR {brand}.
DISTINGUISH CAREFULLY: - "Criteria FOR {brand}" = what the patient must do to ACCESS {brand}. These should be extracted. - "{brand} appears in ANOTHER drug's criteria as a prerequisite" = {brand} is listed as a drug the patient must have ALREADY tried before getting that other drug. These should NOT be extracted for {brand} itself.
DETECTION: If you see language like: "For [OTHER DRUG]: Patient has tried TWO of Enbrel, Humira, {brand}, Skyrizi..." → This tells you what patients need before OTHER DRUG, not what they need before {brand}. {brand} here is a prerequisite for ANOTHER drug, not the target. Return NA if {brand}'s OWN criteria cannot be found separately.
SAFE CHECK: Before extracting, confirm the criteria section is titled for or explicitly applies to {brand} or {generics_list}, not to another drug that lists {brand} as a prerequisite.

DO NOT MIX SUB-OPTIONS FROM DIFFERENT OR BRANCHES.
When a single criterion lists multiple sub-options separated by OR (e.g., "ONE of: oral therapy (MTX, cyclosporine, acitretin) OR PUVA OR biologic (Humira, Remicade)"), the patient only needs ONE sub-option to satisfy that single criterion. These are ALTERNATIVES, not cumulative.
WRONG (do not do this): - Counting the biologic sub-option toward brands=1 AND SIMULTANEOUSLY - Counting the oral therapy sub-option toward generic=1 Result: num_steps_brands=1 AND num_steps_generic=1 — WRONG.
CORRECT (do this instead): - Apply Rule 3: choose the LEAST RESTRICTIVE single sub-option. - If oral therapy OR biologic OR contraindication path exist at equal level: check for 0-step alternatives first. If a contraindication escape exists (e.g., "OR patient has contraindication to one oral agent"), that = 0 steps for that criterion → relevant step parameter = NA. - If no 0-step alternative: choose the least restrictive sub-option for each parameter SEPARATELY.
SPECIFICALLY: if the OR group contains a path where NO biologic is required, num_steps_brands = NA. If it contains a path where NO conventional agent is required, num_steps_generic = NA. Assess each parameter independently.

PARENTHETICAL MODIFIER (narrow exception, NOT a 0-step path): - "(or is not a candidate)" within a step requirement - "(unless contraindicated)" within a step requirement - "(or clinically significant adverse effects are experienced)" within a requirement These are narrow medical exceptions embedded WITHIN a step requirement. They allow the prescriber to waive that specific step for specific patients, but they do NOT create a freestanding alternative path. Do NOT treat these as 0-step paths. Still count the step.
EQUAL-LEVEL OR CLAUSE (true 0-step path via Rule 3): - "OR has an FDA labeled contraindication to ALL conventional agents" — a SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT clause at the SAME grammatical level as the failure requirement. This IS an equal-level OR. Apply Rule 3 → relevant step = NA. - "OR has severe active PsO (≥10% BSA)" — disease severity at equal level. - "OR contraindication to phototherapy, acitretin, cyclosporine, and methotrexate" — equal-level OR clause removing all step requirements.
KEY TEST: Is the contraindication/exception stated as a SEPARATE NUMBERED or BULLETED OPTION at the same level as the failure option? If yes = equal-level OR = 0-step path. If it is embedded in parentheses or after "unless" within a single sentence = parenthetical modifier = still counts as a step.

Some multi-drug policies have TWO layers of step therapy that BOTH apply to {brand}:
LAYER 1 — GENERAL criteria: numbered requirements applying to all drugs in the formulary (e.g., "Criteria 1. BSA ≥3%", "Criteria 2. Three-month trial of oral agent OR phototherapy"). These are necessary but NOT sufficient for {brand}.
LAYER 2 — DRUG-SPECIFIC criteria: a separate numbered subsection naming {brand} or {generics_list} explicitly and adding ADDITIONAL requirements on top of Layer 1 (e.g., "5. For Guselkumab, Ustekinumab: a. Criteria 1 and 2 are applicable; HOWEVER, member must demonstrate failure of BOTH oral agent AND phototherapy... b. Member must fail ALL preferred anti-TNF agents...").
When both layers exist, the step therapy for {brand} is the COMBINATION of both layers — not just one or the other. Look for language like: - "For {brand} / {generics_list}:" - "Coverage Criteria X through Y are applicable; HOWEVER..." - "Additional requirement for {generics_list}:"
When Layer 2 changes an OR to an AND (e.g., "must fail BOTH oral agent AND phototherapy"), the AND version overrides. Set step_phototherapy = "Yes".

example.description: Severity bypass present — return NA for all step parameters
example.policy_excerpt: For plaque psoriasis, the patient meets ONE of the following: 1. Patient has severe active PsO (e.g., greater than 10% BSA, hands/feet/ scalp/face/genitals, intractable pruritus, serious emotional consequences) 2. Patient has concomitant severe PsA (erosive disease, elevated ESR/CRP) 3. Patient has failed ONE conventional agent (methotrexate, cyclosporine, acitretin, topical corticosteroids, PUVA) used in the treatment of PsO after at least a 3-month duration of therapy 4. Patient has an intolerance to ONE conventional agent 5. Patient has an FDA labeled contraindication to ALL conventional agents
example.reasoning: Rule 3: Check ALL branches for 0-step paths FIRST. Options 1 and 2 are severity paths requiring NO prior treatment — these are 0-step paths at equal grammatical level to options 3-5. Under Rule 3 (least restrictive): options 1 and 2 = 0 steps → num_steps_generic = NA. Phototherapy (PUVA) appears only within option 3 alongside oral agents (OR within option 3), and the whole criterion is itself in an OR group (options 1-5). The non-phototherapy path is less restrictive → step_phototherapy = "No". No biologic prerequisite → num_steps_brands = NA.
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "For plaque psoriasis, ONE of: (1) severe active PsO [>10% BSA, crucial body areas, intractable pruritus, serious emotional consequences]; (2) concomitant severe PsA; (3) failed ONE conventional agent [MTX, cyclosporine, acitretin, topicals, PUVA] ≥3 months; (4) intolerance to ONE conventional agent; (5) FDA labeled contraindication to ALL conventional agents.", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "No", "_reasoning": "Options 1 and 2 are equal-level 0-step severity paths; Rule 3 yields NA for all step parameters." }

example.policy_excerpt:
Patient meets ALL of the following ¥: - Patient did not respond adequately (or is not a candidate) to a 4-week minimum trial of topical agents; AND - Patient did not respond adequately (or is not a candidate) to a 3-month minimum trial of at least one non-biologic systemic agent; AND - Patient did not respond adequately (or is not a candidate) to a 3-month minimum trial of phototherapy (PUVA or UVB)
¥ Note: For patients already established on biologic therapy, targeted synthetic therapy, or those with >10% BSA involvement, trial and failure of topical agents, non-biologic systemic agents, and phototherapy is NOT required.
example.reasoning: The ¥-note creates a complete 0-step path for patients with >10% BSA or existing biologic therapy. Under Rule 3 (least restrictive), this blanket exception means all step parameters = NA, photo = "No". The "(or is not a candidate)" are parenthetical modifiers within each step — they do NOT create independent 0-step paths. The ¥-note DOES create one.
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "Patient must have tried topical agents AND non-biologic systemic agent AND phototherapy — BUT: ¥ For patients with >10% BSA or established on biologic therapy, ALL step therapy requirements are waived.", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "No", "_reasoning": "¥-note creates a complete 0-step path for common moderate-severe PsO patients (>10% BSA); Rule 3 yields NA for all step parameters." }

example.description: Step Table — non-preferred drug requiring TWO preferred biologics
example.policy_excerpt:
Step Table for Plaque Psoriasis: Step 1a (Preferred): adalimumab products, Cosentyx, Enbrel, Otezla, Skyrizi, Stelara, Tremfya Step 3a (Non-Preferred, directed to TWO Step 1 agents): Bimzelx, Cimzia, ILUMYA
For Ilumya (plaque psoriasis): d. Member meets ONE of the following (indication criteria): i. Therapeutic failure or intolerance to phototherapy (PUVA, UVB) ii. Therapeutic failure or intolerance to at least one systemic therapy (e.g., methotrexate) iii. Contraindicated to BOTH phototherapy AND systemic therapy e. Therapeutic failure or intolerance to at least two (2) step 1 or 2 plan-preferred agents for PsO.
example.reasoning: ILUMYA is at Step 3a → 2 preferred biologic/targeted agents required (criterion e). No "contraindication to ALL" escape stated for criterion e → brands=2 (hard requirement). For indication criteria (criterion d): - Option iii (contraindicated to BOTH phototherapy AND systemic therapy) = equal-level OR at same level as i and ii → 0-step path for generics under Rule 3 → generic=NA. - Under Rule 6: phototherapy in OR with systemic therapy → photo=No.
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "Step 3a non-preferred. Indication criteria: ONE of (i) phototherapy failure/intolerance; (ii) ONE systemic therapy failure/intolerance; (iii) contraindicated to BOTH phototherapy AND systemic therapy. PLUS: failure/intolerance to at least TWO step 1 or 2 preferred agents.", "num_steps_brands": "2", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "No", "_reasoning": "Step Table places ILUMYA at Step 3a (brands=2). Indication option iii is equal-level 0-step escape for generics. Phototherapy in OR group → No." }

example.description: Wrong-section extraction — brand appears as prerequisite for another drug
example.policy_excerpt:
For Cimzia — Plaque Psoriasis: Patient has tried TWO of Enbrel, adalimumab product, Otezla, Skyrizi, Stelara subcutaneous, Taltz, or TREMFYA.
For Enbrel — All Conditions: Approve if patient meets the standard Inflammatory Conditions - Enbrel Prior Authorization Policy criteria.
example.reasoning: Extracting for ENBREL. The "tried TWO of Enbrel, ... Tremfya" text is CIMZIA's prerequisites — Enbrel appears there as one of the drugs Cimzia patients must have tried. This is NOT the criteria FOR Enbrel. Enbrel's own criteria say "standard Inflammatory Conditions - Enbrel PA criteria" (referenced elsewhere). Since no explicit step therapy is stated for Enbrel in this document, return NA for all step fields.
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "NA", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "NA", "_reasoning": "Enbrel appears in Cimzia's prerequisites (as a drug Cimzia patients must have tried), not in its own PA criteria. Enbrel's criteria reference a separate standard policy not in this document." }

example.description: Brand is PREFERRED — return NA for all fields
example.policy_excerpt: Preferred products: Cosentyx, Enbrel, Humira, Stelara, Tremfya... Non-preferred (targeted): Cimzia, Ilumya, Remicade... Exception criteria (for non-preferred products): 1. Inadequate response to a preferred product 2. Contraindication to all preferred products
example.reasoning: STELARA appears in the PREFERRED list. The exception criteria are for patients accessing non-preferred drugs. No step therapy applies to STELARA itself. Return NA for all.
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "NA", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "NA", "_reasoning": "Stelara is listed as a Preferred product in this policy; the exception criteria apply to non-preferred drugs only." }

example.description: OR-path mixing prevention — three equal-level paths, one is 0-step
example.policy_excerpt: Patient meets ONE of the following: (i) Has tried at least one of the following for ≥3 months: oral therapy (MTX, cyclosporine, acitretin); oral methoxsalen plus UVA (PUVA); or a biologic (Humira, Remicade, Stelara) (ii) Experienced an intolerance to at least one oral or biologic therapy (iii) Has a contraindication to one oral agent for psoriasis (e.g., MTX)
example.reasoning: Three equal-level OR paths: (i), (ii), (iii). Path (iii): contraindication to ONE oral agent = prescriber determination, no drug trial needed → 0-step path at equal level. Rule 3: path (iii) = 0 steps → num_steps_generic = NA, num_steps_brands = NA. WRONG approach (do not do): apply biologic sub-option of path (i) → brands=1 AND oral sub-option of path (i) → generic=1 simultaneously. This is OR-path mixing — the patient needs only ONE of the sub-options within path (i).
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "Patient meets ONE of: (i) tried ≥3 months of oral therapy (MTX/cyclosporine/acitretin), PUVA, or biologic (Humira/Remicade/Stelara); (ii) intolerance to oral or biologic therapy; (iii) contraindication to one oral agent (e.g., MTX).", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "NA", "step_phototherapy": "No", "_reasoning": "Path (iii) is equal-level 0-step escape; Rule 3 → NA for both brands and generic. Phototherapy in OR group within path (i) → No." }

example.policy_excerpt: Patient must have tried and failed phototherapy (UVB or PUVA) AND at least one conventional systemic agent (methotrexate, cyclosporine, or acitretin).
example.output: { "step_therapy_text": "Patient must have tried and failed phototherapy (UVB or PUVA) AND at least one conventional systemic agent (methotrexate, cyclosporine, or acitretin).", "num_steps_brands": "NA", "num_steps_generic": "1", "step_phototherapy": "Yes", "_reasoning": "Phototherapy and conventional agent are joined by AND — both are mandatory. No severity bypass or OR escape present." }
